artworks.title: Aeneas, Anchises, and Ascanius
artworks.description: Bernini's early Borghese marble stacks three generations in flight from Troy: Ascanius follows at his father's heel while Aeneas bears Anchises — the boy who will found Alba Longa already walking out of the sack.

artworks.title: Ascanius Shooting the Stag of Sylvia
artworks.description: Claude's late Ashmolean landscape restages Aeneid 7: Ascanius' arrow kills Silvia's stag and lights the war in Latium — the boy's hunt as the spark that turns Trojan refugees into Italian enemies.

artworks.title: Aeneas' Flight from Troy
artworks.description: Barocci's Borghese canvas keeps Ascanius beside his father in the burning city — the small heir of the Julian line escaping with Anchises on Aeneas' shoulders.

music.title: Ascanio in Alba
music.description: Mozart's festa teatrale for Milan crowns Ascanius (Ascanio) as the young founder of Alba — Virgil's boy given an opera of Venus, nymphs, and dynastic marriage.

popCulture.title: Aeneid
popCulture.creator: Virgil
popCulture.description: Virgil's epic makes Ascanius — also Iulus — the living pledge of Rome: the child who flees Troy, founds Alba, and lends his name to the Julian house.

popCulture.title: Ascanius
popCulture.description: Aeneas' son, legendary founder of Alba Longa — the Trojan boy whose other name, Iulus, Rome's rulers claimed as their own.
